lesson.regexForSeo.starter.title: Regex for SEO
lesson.regexForSeo.starter.description: Regex (regular expressions) is a pattern language frequently used in many fields, especially by people who want to work more efficiently. Using Regex for SEO makes it easier to analyze large amounts of data and write richer filters. We recommend starting with the `Regex 101` tutorial if you are new to Regex.\n\nStart by typing `OK` in the Regex field to proceed to the first step and access more detailed explanations.
lesson.regexForSeo.usage.title: Use Cases
lesson.regexForSeo.usage.description: You can use Regex for SEO on platforms such as `Google Analytics`, `Google Data Studio`, `Google Sheets`, `Google Search Console`, `Ahrefs`, `Deepcrawl`, `Screaming Frog`. It is also frequently used in `.htaccess` and `robots.txt (regex-like syntax)` files.\n\nBelow is a sample regex that will select only texts in the list that start with `Google`.
lesson.regexForSeo.basics.title: Basics
lesson.regexForSeo.basics.description: Let's take a look at some regex patterns you will use often. To learn more about them, we recommend the `Regex 101` tutorial. Type `Yes` to get started.
lesson.regexForSeo.or.title: Or Operator `|`
lesson.regexForSeo.or.description: We use the Or operator `|` to filter for multiple expressions. For example, to filter text containing `seo` or `regex`, write both words separated by the Or operator `|`.
lesson.regexForSeo.optional.title: Optional Operator `?`
lesson.regexForSeo.optional.description: We use it to express that a character or expression is optional. For example, we want to filter text containing either `http` or `https`. We could use the Or operator `|` for this, but there is a better way for these two almost identical words.\n\nIn this example, the letter `s` is optional. Add a question mark `?` after the letter `s`.
lesson.regexForSeo.any.title: Anything `.*`
lesson.regexForSeo.any.description: In regex, the period `.` matches any single character, including spaces. The asterisk `*` means the preceding item can occur zero or more times. Used together, `.*` matches any sequence of characters of any length.\n\nBelow are various keywords. Add `.*` to the end of the regex to write the expression that starts with `how to write` and matches everything after it.
lesson.regexForSeo.contains.title: Contains
lesson.regexForSeo.contains.description: To filter text that contains a word or phrase, we write it between two `.*` patterns, which match everything. For example, type `.*buy.*` to filter for text that includes `buy`.
lesson.regexForSeo.negated.title: Negated Character Sets `[^abc]`
lesson.regexForSeo.negated.description: We use negated character sets `[^abc]` to specify characters that must not appear. The characters are written inside square brackets, starting with a caret `^`. Below are both `http` and `https`. Since `http` appears in both, it also matches `https`. Type `[^s]` after the letter `p` to exclude the letter `s`.
lesson.regexForSeo.caret.title: Caret Sign `^`
lesson.regexForSeo.caret.description: Let's say we have a list of URLs, and we want to find only those URLs that start with `http`. But URLs also contain `http` in different parts other than their beginning. Add a caret `^` to the beginning of the following expression to filter only those starting with `http`.
lesson.regexForSeo.dollarAndEscape.title: Dollar Sign `$` and Escape Character `\`
lesson.regexForSeo.dollarAndEscape.descr:
Again we have a list of URLs. We want to find only those URLs ending in `.htm`.

Since the period `.` is a special character that matches everything, we first need to escape the period before `htm` with the escape character `\`. This applies to all special characters.

Then add a `$` sign to the end of the expression. This ensures that the text to be filtered ends with the expression written before it.
lesson.regexForSeo.limitation.title: Length Restrictions `{n}`
lesson.regexForSeo.limitation.descriptio: We may want to filter results by their length. For example, to filter URLs that are exactly `35` characters long, add the length in curly braces `{35}` right after the period `.`.
lesson.regexForSeo.maxLimitation.title: Length Restrictions (Maximum) `{n,m}`
lesson.regexForSeo.maxLimitation.descrip: To filter URLs that are at most `35` characters long, add the minimum and maximum length in curly braces `{1,35}` right after the period `.`.
lesson.regexForSeo.minLimitation.title: Length Restrictions (Minimum) `{n,}`
lesson.regexForSeo.minLimitation.descrip: To filter URLs that are at least `35` characters long, add the minimum length followed by a comma in curly braces `{35,}` right after the period `.`.
lesson.regexForSeo.robots.title: robots.txt (regex-like syntax)
lesson.regexForSeo.robots.description: Here is an example of regex-like usage in the `robots.txt` file. The example states that bots should not crawl links with the extension `pdf`.
lesson.regexForSeo.htaccess.title: .htaccess
lesson.regexForSeo.htaccess.description: Here is an example of using regex in the `.htaccess` file. In the example, links with the `php` extension are redirected to their `html` versions with a `301` redirect.
lesson.regexForSeo.outro.title: Outro
lesson.regexForSeo.outro.description: Regex knowledge is a skill that increases productivity on any platform that allows you to use regex. Once you start using it and improve this skill, it will help you complete many repetitive tasks faster and save time for other things. To better understand the basics of Regex, you can visit the `Regex 101` tutorial. You can use the `Playground` page to test your own expressions on your own text.
